messages.help.my_account.title: My Account
messages.help.my_account.intro: My Account is your own profile. What you change here applies to your account only.
messages.help.my_account.intro.open: Sign-in is off, so DebridPulse is used as its built-in Administrator, and this is that account.
messages.help.my_account.profile.username: DP Username is the name your account signs in with when it uses a local password. It is separate from your display name, and only an Admin can change it.
messages.help.my_account.profile.display_name: Display Name is the name DebridPulse shows for you.
messages.help.my_account.profile.actual_name: Actual Name is your full name, if you want to record it. It is profile information only: it never signs you in or decides what you may do.
messages.help.my_account.profile.email.own: Email: while none is recorded you may enter one; it is stored as unverified. An email you entered yourself can be corrected with the pencil beside it. An email never signs you in, links accounts, or grants anything.
messages.help.my_account.profile.email.provider: Email: your identity provider supplied it, so it is shown read-only here. An email never signs you in, links accounts, or grants anything.
messages.help.my_account.profile.save: Save saves your changes to the names and the email; Cancel leaves them as they were.
messages.help.my_account.password.change: Change Password asks for your current password and a new one, entered twice. They are never shown or kept after the dialog closes.
messages.help.my_account.password.change.sessions: Saving the new password ends your browser sessions; where sign-in is required, sign in again with it.
messages.help.my_account.password.first: Your account has no local password: it signs in through your identity provider. Set Password gives it one, under your DP Username.
messages.help.my_account.password.first.enabled: That password works for sign-in only while an Admin has Username & Password sign-in enabled.
messages.help.my_account.password.standalone_firs: Set Password gives the built-in Administrator its password.
Saving it also turns on password sign-in: from then on DebridPulse asks for this password, and only this password, before anyone can use it.
messages.help.my_account.signin.required: Password required to sign in: password sign-in is on now, so DebridPulse asks for your password before anyone can use it.
messages.help.my_account.signin.not_required: No password required to sign in: sign-in is off now, so anyone who can reach DebridPulse can use it as the built-in Administrator.
messages.help.my_account.signin.reading: This line says whether sign-in is required now. It is not a reading of whether a password is stored.
messages.help.my_account.clear.steps: Clear Password asks for your current password and then a confirmation. It removes your password and turns password sign-in off, together.
messages.help.my_account.presentation.choice: Easy | Advanced chooses how much of the interface you see. Advanced, the default, shows the full interface your role and this installation’s deployment type allow; Easy hides further advanced pages, cards, and tuning.
messages.help.my_account.presentation.admin_examp: In Easy, for example, the Activity Log and Settings cards such as Transfer Method Settings, Event Logging, and Database Reset Controls are hidden.
messages.help.my_account.presentation.user_exampl: In Easy, for example, the Statistics Reporting card of your Notifications is hidden.
messages.help.my_account.presentation.unchanged: It changes only what is shown. Your role and permissions, your saved settings, and everything DebridPulse does in the background stay the same, and settings you no longer see keep working with their saved values. Choosing Advanced never adds anything your role or the deployment type does not allow.
messages.help.my_account.presentation.saved: Your choice applies at once, without Save, and is saved to your account, so it follows you to every browser.
messages.help.my_account.presentation.open: While sign-in is off it belongs to the built-in Administrator, so every browser of this installation shows the same choice.

messages.help.quickstart.title: Getting started with DebridPulse
messages.help.quickstart.summary.admin: Four short steps from a fresh installation to your first finished download.
messages.help.quickstart.lead.debridpulse_applica: DebridPulse is the application you use to submit, route, track, and manage downloads. You give it a link, a magnet, or a file such as a {file_type_1}, {file_type_2} or Metalink file. DebridPulse works out which of your services can fetch it, downloads the files to your storage with the right download engine, and keeps track of every download until it finishes.
messages.help.quickstart.lead.do_not_need: You do not need a paid account to start. Ordinary web (HTTP and HTTPS), FTP, SFTP, SCP, rsync and WebDAV links, Metalink files and supported media pages work without one. Torrents, magnets, file-hoster links and NZBs need a service you already have an account with, such as a debrid service (a paid online service that fetches torrents and file-hoster downloads for you) or a Usenet news server.
messages.help.quickstart.before_begin.storage: Storage: DebridPulse needs a folder it is allowed to write to. This can be a folder on the computer running DebridPulse or a mounted network share.
messages.help.quickstart.before_begin.login_prote: Login protection: A new installation does not ask anyone to sign in. If people or devices you do not fully trust can reach DebridPulse, open My Account and use Set Password: DebridPulse then asks for that password before anyone can use it.
messages.help.quickstart.before_begin.who_can_do_: Who can do what: only the built-in Administrator can sign in to a Standalone installation, and it manages Settings. Other people's accounts, kept from a time this installation was a Server, are not deleted or converted: they keep their data but cannot sign in while it is Standalone. Other applications connect as Integration accounts, under Settings → Access & Integrations.
messages.help.quickstart.before_begin.login_prote: Login protection: If people or devices you do not fully trust can reach DebridPulse, open Settings → Authentication first and set up Username & Password. A new installation does not ask anyone to sign in.

Login protection: If people or devices you do not fully trust can reach DebridPulse, set up Username & Password first, in Settings → Authentication; its card is shown when My Account is set to Advanced. A new installation does not ask anyone to sign in.
messages.help.quickstart.before_begin.who_can_do_: Who can do what: these steps are for an Admin, the role that manages Settings. Other people can have their own accounts with the User or ReadOnly User role; see Everyday Use.
messages.help.quickstart.check_where_downloads.op: Open Settings → Downloads → Download Behavior & Limits and look at Download Folder. The usual value is {path}. Browse lets you pick a folder and shows how much free space it has.
messages.help.quickstart.check_where_downloads.if: If DebridPulse runs in Docker, it lives in an isolated environment called a container, and {path} is the folder as DebridPulse sees it inside that container. Your installation connects it to a real folder on your computer, NAS or server. If files already arrive where you expect, leave this setting alone.
messages.help.quickstart.choose_services_want.ope: Open Settings → Services. The Network Sources group (HTTP(S), (S)FTP, SCP, rsync, WebDAV, Metalink (Multimeta) and Media Downloads) is switched on in a new installation, so ordinary links work straight away.
messages.help.quickstart.choose_services_want.eve: Every Premium Service is switched off in a new installation, and none is required. To use a premium service, open its card under Premium Services, switch it on with Enable, and connect your account:
messages.help.quickstart.choose_services_want.all: AllDebrid, Debrid-Link and Premiumize: paste the API key from your account into API Key. An API key is a private code that lets DebridPulse use your account without your password.
messages.help.quickstart.choose_services_want.rea: Real-Debrid and TorBox: press Connect Real-Debrid or Connect TorBox, then approve the code on the service's own website.
messages.help.quickstart.choose_services_want.use: Usenet: add your news server with Add Server.
messages.help.quickstart.choose_services_want.pre: Press Test on the card to check the connection. The Services tab of this manual describes every service.
messages.help.quickstart.add_first_download.dashb: On the Dashboard, paste a link into Quick Add and press Add. Put each download on its own line. To add a file instead, leave the box empty and press Add to choose a {file_type_1}, {file_type_2}, {file_type_3} or a text file that lists links.
messages.help.quickstart.add_first_download.if_do: If the download contains several files, DebridPulse may ask you which ones you want. If a server needs a password, it asks for one.
messages.help.quickstart.follow_finish.download_a: The download appears in Download Activity on the Dashboard and in Downloads. Click it to open its details: the service delivering it, its files, and its events.
messages.help.quickstart.follow_finish.if_somethi: If something does not go as expected, read the download's details and, as an Admin, the Activity Log before deleting anything. The Troubleshooting tab starts from common symptoms.
If something does not go as expected, read the download's details and its events before deleting anything. The Troubleshooting tab starts from common symptoms.
messages.help.quickstart.where_read_next.everyday: Everyday Use: every page, button and prompt you will meet day to day.
messages.help.quickstart.where_read_next.how_work: How It Works: how a service is chosen, what happens when something fails, and what pausing, retrying and removing do.
messages.help.quickstart.where_read_next.services: Services and Engines: what each service and engine can and cannot do.
messages.help.quickstart.where_read_next.settings: Settings: every Settings tab, card and important option. In Settings itself, the Help button (?) on each card explains that card.
messages.help.quickstart.where_read_next.optional: Optional features such as automatic archive extraction, webhook notifications, backups and a sign-in password can be added whenever you need them.
Optional features such as automatic archive extraction, webhook notifications, backups and OpenID Connect sign-in can be added whenever you need them.
messages.help.using.title: Using DebridPulse
messages.help.using.summary: The pages, controls and prompts you use every day, in the order you meet them.
messages.help.using.lead.sidebar_has_three.activi: The sidebar has three groups: Queue (Dashboard and Downloads), Review (Activity Log and Statistics) and System (Settings and Help & License). The number beside Downloads counts downloads that are still in progress, waiting or paused; failed and finished ones are not counted.
messages.help.using.lead.sidebar_has_three.admin: The sidebar has three groups: Queue (Dashboard and Downloads), Review (Statistics) and System (Settings and Help & License). The number beside Downloads counts downloads that are still in progress, waiting or paused; failed and finished ones are not counted.
messages.help.using.lead.sidebar_has_three.person: The sidebar has three groups: Queue (Dashboard and Downloads), Review (Statistics) and System (Notifications and Help & License). The number beside Downloads counts downloads that are still in progress, waiting or paused; failed and finished ones are not counted.
messages.help.using.lead.sidebar_has_three.no_per: The sidebar has three groups: Queue (Dashboard and Downloads), Review (Statistics) and System (Help & License). The number beside Downloads counts downloads that are still in progress, waiting or paused; failed and finished ones are not counted.
messages.help.using.lead.standalone_installation_: On a Standalone installation only the built-in Administrator signs in, and the interface is the Standalone one: it has no Authentication tab and no User Accounts card. Integration accounts still connect other applications.
messages.help.using.lead.what_see_depends: What you see depends on your role. Settings, the Activity Log and the controls marked Admin only below appear only for an Admin; a User sees Notifications in place of Settings, and a ReadOnly User can look but not change anything.
messages.help.using.lead.presentation_easy_so: Your presentation is Easy, so some advanced pages, cards and tuning are hidden. Advanced, chosen in My Account, shows the full interface your role and this installation's deployment type allow; neither changes what you may do.
messages.help.using.who_uses_installation.built_a: The built-in Administrator is the only person who can sign in. It has the Admin's pages and controls described here, as a Standalone installation presents them: Settings, Pause All, the speed cap, Provider Status, Recover All and every download.
messages.help.using.who_uses_installation.other_p: Other people's accounts, kept from a time this installation was a Server, are not deleted or converted. They keep their data but cannot sign in while it is Standalone.
messages.help.using.who_uses_installation.integra: Integration accounts are for other applications. They use API tokens and cannot sign in to these pages.
messages.help.using.who_uses_installation.my_acco: My Account, opened from the account control in the sidebar, changes the display name and actual name, sets, changes or clears the password, and chooses Easy or Advanced. Log Out appears beside it while sign-in is on.
messages.help.using.what_role_lets.admin: Admin: everything, including Settings, the Activity Log, Pause All, the speed cap, Provider Status, Recover All and every download.
messages.help.using.what_role_lets.user: User: adds downloads, and pauses, resumes, retries and reorders them. Removing, cancelling or switching the source of a download is allowed only when no other account still needs it; otherwise you can withdraw your own request from the download's details (Requested By). Your own Discord alerts and statistics reports are under Notifications.
messages.help.using.what_role_lets.readonly_user: ReadOnly User: sees the Dashboard, Downloads, download details and Statistics, and changes nothing in downloads or settings; its own profile and presentation in My Account remain its own to change.
messages.help.using.what_role_lets.name_bottom_si: Your name at the bottom of the sidebar opens My Account, where you can change your display name and, if you sign in with one, your password. Log Out is beside it.
messages.help.using.what_role_lets.my_account_eas: My Account's Easy | Advanced chooses how much of the interface you see; it is saved to your account.
messages.help.using.header_controls.pause_all: Pause All (Admin only): pauses every download and stops DebridPulse from starting new work. You can still add downloads while paused; they wait in the queue. The button then reads Resume All, which resumes everything, including downloads you paused one by one.
messages.help.using.header_controls.resume_paused: Resume Paused (N) (Admin only): appears when processing is running but some downloads are individually paused. It resumes them all.
messages.help.using.header_controls.activity_badg: Activity badge: shows how many downloads are running out of the maximum allowed, the current combined speed, and the speed cap. An Admin can open its menu to pick a cap (Unlimited, 1, 5, 10, 20, 30, 50 or 100 MB/s), or type one in Custom cap (MB/s) and press Set Custom. The cap covers every download together, whichever engine runs it, and stays in place after a restart.
Activity badge: shows the current combined download speed and the speed cap, which an Admin sets for every download together.
messages.help.using.header_controls.when_admin_pa: When an Admin pauses all processing, downloads wait without starting until it is resumed.
messages.help.using.header_controls.theme_button: Theme button: switches between dark and light mode.
messages.help.using.header_controls.while_downloa: While downloads are running, the browser tab title shows the overall speed and progress.
messages.help.using.provider_status_sidebar.sideb: The sidebar lists your services with a coloured dot. The colour is the whole message:
messages.help.using.provider_status_sidebar.green: Green: working. For a premium service this also means its current settings have passed a Test.
messages.help.using.provider_status_sidebar.amber: Amber: usable but limited. For example: switched on but not set up yet, not tested since its settings changed, or connected to a free or expired account.
messages.help.using.provider_status_sidebar.red: Red: not usable. For example: the sign-in was rejected, the service is unavailable, or it is switched off.
messages.help.using.provider_status_sidebar.pulsi: Pulsing amber: still checking, or not known yet.
messages.help.using.provider_status_sidebar.netwo: Network Sources share one row. If a status check briefly fails, DebridPulse keeps showing the last good answer for up to five minutes rather than flashing red, as long as that service's settings have not changed. A premium account's expiry is shown above the services. The aria2 engine and the database appear only when they report a problem (for example aria2: offline), and the DebridPulse version is shown at the bottom of the sidebar.
messages.help.using.dashboard_quick_add.summary_c: The summary cards count Total Downloads, Completed, Active Now, Processing, Errors and Total Downloaded. Click Errors to open Downloads filtered to failed downloads.
messages.help.using.dashboard_quick_add.links: Links: {link_1}, {link_2}, {link_3}, {link_4}, {link_5}, {link_6}, {link_7}, {link_8}, {link_9}, {link_10}, {link_11} and {link_12}. One download per line; up to 100 different links at once (magnets are not counted). Exact duplicate lines are ignored.
messages.help.using.dashboard_quick_add.magnet_li: Magnet links (they start with {link}), one per line.
messages.help.using.dashboard_quick_add.alternate: Alternate sources: put several links for the same item on one line, separated by a Tab. DebridPulse treats them as one download and tries the next link on that line only if the previous one fails.
messages.help.using.dashboard_quick_add.press_add: Press Add (or Ctrl+Enter). If a line is not a link or magnet DebridPulse recognises, nothing is added and the message names that line. If the server refuses some entries, the others are still added and the message counts how many failed. Lines that could not be added stay in the box.
messages.help.using.dashboard_quick_add.add_file_: To add a file, empty the box and press Add. The file's name decides what it is:
messages.help.using.dashboard_quick_add.torrent_t: {file_type}: a torrent file, up to 16 MB.
messages.help.using.dashboard_quick_add.nzb_usene: {file_type}: a Usenet download, up to 1 GB.
messages.help.using.dashboard_quick_add.meta4_met: {file_type}: a Metalink file, up to 16 MB.
messages.help.using.dashboard_quick_add.any_other: Any other file: read as a list of links, up to 1 MB. Plain text with one link per line works; so do simple JSON, XML or YAML lists. Lines beginning with {literal} are ignored.
messages.help.using.dashboard_quick_add.recover_a: Recover All (Admin only), in the Quick Add header, asks DebridPulse to check all tracked work and pick up anything that can safely continue. See the How It Works tab.
messages.help.using.dashboard_quick_add.download_: Download Activity shows the downloads at the top of the queue with their status, progress, size and date. Admins and Users can pause or resume them there; click a row to open its details, or View All to open Downloads.
Download Activity shows the downloads at the top of the queue with their status, progress, size and date. Click a row to open its details, or View All to open Downloads.
messages.help.using.questions_debridpulse_may.con: Connect to a local network address? appears when a link points at a device on your private network and Local Network Connections is on (unless Skip Local Connection Confirmation is also on). Allow applies to that download only. When Local Network Connections is off, such links are refused.
messages.help.using.questions_debridpulse_may.dow: Download the item or its collection? appears when a link points at one item inside a collection, for example a video that is part of a playlist. Choose the item, the whole collection, or Cancel Transfer.
messages.help.using.questions_debridpulse_may.aut: Authentication Required appears when a server needs a username and password, or, for SSH-based servers, a key file and its passphrase. Cancel, when shown, cancels the download.
messages.help.using.questions_debridpulse_may.ver: Verify Server Identity appears before DebridPulse first connects to an SFTP, SCP or SSH server whose identity has not been confirmed yet. Compare the fingerprint shown with the one the server's owner gave you, then press Verify & Continue.
messages.help.using.questions_debridpulse_may.the: These dialogs do not close when you click outside them; choose one of their buttons.
messages.help.using.choosing_files.when_torrent_m: When a torrent, magnet, Metalink file or folder link contains more than one file, Select files opens automatically once the file list is known. Every file starts ticked. Untick what you do not want and press Confirm.
messages.help.using.choosing_files.if_do_nothing: If you do nothing, every file downloads when the countdown ends. Close also keeps all files.
messages.help.using.choosing_files.can_reopen_sel: You can reopen the selection later with Choose Files or Change Files on the download, while it can still be changed.
messages.help.using.choosing_files.collection_sep: For a collection of separate items (titled Select entries), nothing downloads until you confirm, and Close cancels the download.
messages.help.using.choosing_files.nzb_downloads_: NZB downloads always fetch the whole posting; there is no file selection.
messages.help.using.downloads_page.filters: Filters: All, Downloading, Paused, Processing, Ready, Done, Error. Search matches as you type.
messages.help.using.downloads_page.row_actions: Row actions: Pause, Resume, Retry (on a failed download) and Remove. Start Now appears when a download you moved up can only start if lower downloads restart. For a User, Remove appears only on downloads no other account still needs.
messages.help.using.downloads_page.several_once: Several at once: tick rows to show Pause, Resume, Reset (retry), Move to Top and Delete. Delete is offered only when you may remove every selected download.
messages.help.using.downloads_page.queue_order: Queue order: in Priority order with no filter or search, drag a download by its name to move it, or use the keyboard (Space or Enter to pick up, arrow keys to move, Space or Enter to drop, Escape to cancel). Right-click offers Move to Top. If a move would interrupt a running download, DebridPulse asks first because that download's progress would be lost.
messages.help.using.downloads_page.beneath_each_n: Beneath each name, the row shows where the download came from and which service is handling it (how it was submitted is in its details). Where you may change it, the service name is a button that opens the service picker. A network icon with a number shows how many sources are known for its files; when another source can be chosen it is a button that opens the source chooser. Both are explained under How It Works → Switching service or source.
messages.help.using.downloads_page.date_column_me: The Date column's menu sets the date format and 12- or 24-hour time, for Downloads and the Dashboard.
messages.help.using.download_details.click_any_do: Click any download to open its details.
messages.help.using.download_details.provider: Provider is the service handling the download now. Submitted As is what you gave DebridPulse (for example Direct link, Magnet link, Torrent file, NZB file or Metalink file). Original Resource is the source you submitted.
messages.help.using.download_details.requested: Requested By lists the accounts that asked for this download. A User can withdraw their own request there; the download itself continues while another account still needs it.
messages.help.using.download_details.route_histor: Route History lists every service DebridPulse tried for this download and how each attempt ended.
messages.help.using.download_details.advanced_acq: Advanced acquisition details separates the engine, the service you started with, the current service, and the service that actually delivered the files.
messages.help.using.download_details.files.operat: Files lists each file with its size and status. Depending on the download, its header lets you switch service (Provider), switch the remaining files to another common source, or change the file selection. Each file's Candidates list shows the other sources known for it. If a switch would throw away progress, DebridPulse asks Discard downloaded progress? first.
messages.help.using.download_details.files.viewer: Files lists each file with its size and status. Each file's Candidates list shows the other sources known for it.
messages.help.using.download_details.events.admin: Events is this download's own history. Transfer Trace Log (Admin only) saves a detailed record you can attach to a bug report; DebridPulse removes passwords and private link details from it, but read it before sharing.
messages.help.using.download_details.progress_mar: Progress marked not yet verified or estimated is DebridPulse's best estimate until the files are checked.
messages.help.using.activity_log_admin.activity_l: The Activity Log is the full event history of DebridPulse: transfers, routing decisions, recovery, storage, extraction, settings changes and more. Filter it by Time Window, Severity (Info, Warning, Error) and Event Type, or search for a name or transfer ID. Expand Details on an event for more information.
messages.help.using.activity_log_admin.events_kep: Events are kept until you reset the database. The number shown per page is set in Settings → Data & Maintenance → Event Logging.
messages.help.using.statistics.top_cards_completi: The top cards and the Completions chart follow the Period you choose (1 hour to All Time).
messages.help.using.statistics.overall_rolling_me: Overall & Rolling Metrics always shows the last 24 hours, the last 7 days and lifetime figures.
messages.help.using.statistics.completions_chart_: The Completions chart splits each bar into Premium Sources and Network Sources by the service that actually delivered the files.
messages.help.using.statistics.transfer_methods: Transfer Methods counts finished downloads by how their files were really obtained (for example Debrid, Usenet, HTTP(S), FTP / SFTP, SCP, rsync, WebDAV or Media Downloads), not by what you submitted. A download whose files came by several methods, such as a Metalink download, is counted once under each. Finished downloads with no recorded method appear as Unattributed.
messages.help.using.statistics.transfer_dispositi: Transfer Disposition, File Status and Events Severity count downloads, files and log events by state.
messages.help.howitworks.title: How downloads work
messages.help.howitworks.summary: What DebridPulse does between pressing Add and a finished file, and what it does when something goes wrong.
messages.help.howitworks.lead.each_thing_add: Each thing you add becomes one download that DebridPulse tracks from start to finish, even if it changes service, source or engine along the way. A service (also called a provider or source) is what can obtain the files: a debrid account, a Usenet server, or a network protocol such as HTTPS or rsync. A download engine is the program that writes the files to your storage.
messages.help.howitworks.how_service_chosen.speci: Specialist services come first. A magnet, {file_type} or NZB goes only to services that handle that kind of input. A web link goes to a debrid service only if that service lists the link's host as supported, and while one can take it, the ordinary HTTP(S) source waits. A single web link can still be downloaded directly over HTTP(S) if every debrid service that could take it runs out of retries for it or becomes unavailable.
messages.help.howitworks.how_service_chosen.links: Links added together are one download. All the links you add at once in Quick Add, or in one link-list file, become a single download; only magnets each become a download of their own, and links on one line separated by a Tab are alternatives for the same item. If a debrid service supports any link in a download of two or more links, the whole download is left to debrid services: each of its links goes to a debrid service that supports that particular link, and a link that none of them supports is not downloaded as an ordinary web file, not even later. To download ordinary web links directly, add them separately from links meant for a debrid service. Media Downloads links do not have this effect.
messages.help.howitworks.how_service_chosen.waits: It waits rather than guesses. While a connected debrid service is still loading its list of supported hosts, or its account's features are not known yet, DebridPulse waits for it instead of downloading the link as an ordinary web file.
messages.help.howitworks.how_service_chosen.ready: Ready content is preferred. For torrents, a service that reports the content as already available (TorBox and Premiumize can) is tried before one that would need to fetch it. A service you chose yourself keeps its place.
messages.help.howitworks.how_service_chosen.no_ra: No ranking setting. Settings does not have a general priority order for services; the order of cards in Settings and in the sidebar is only for display. For NZBs, Use TorBox Before Usenet and Use Premiumize Before Usenet let those services try first. You can also choose a service yourself for a download; see Switching service or source below.
messages.help.howitworks.how_service_chosen.enabl: Enabled is not the same as usable. A service that is switched on but not connected, or whose account does not include a feature (for example a free plan), is skipped for that download.
messages.help.howitworks.what_status_words.pendin: Pending, Resolving, Processing: DebridPulse is choosing a service, or a service is preparing the download; no files are arriving yet.
messages.help.howitworks.what_status_words.ready_: Ready, Queued, Waiting for execution slot: ready, but waiting for a free place under Maximum Concurrent Downloads.
messages.help.howitworks.what_status_words.downlo: Downloading, Verifying: files are arriving or being checked.
messages.help.howitworks.what_status_words.waitin: Waiting for provider, Waiting for storage, Waiting for executor, Waiting for retry: held until a service (or a service still preparing it), enough free disk space, an engine or the next retry time is available.
messages.help.howitworks.what_status_words.input_: Input Required: DebridPulse needs an answer from you, such as a password, a server identity check or a file selection.
messages.help.howitworks.what_status_words.awaiti: Awaiting confirmation: DebridPulse is confirming the download's real state with the engine or service, for example after a restart.
messages.help.howitworks.what_status_words.paused: Paused, Recovering: held on purpose, or being picked up again.
messages.help.howitworks.what_status_words.done: Done: finished. Completed with errors or Partial: finished, but some files did not arrive. Consolidated: merged into another download of the same thing. Consolidated · Unverified: DebridPulse could not prove it is the same thing, so nothing was downloaded for it yet; Retry on its unverified source in the other download's details checks again.
messages.help.howitworks.what_status_words.failed: Failed, Requires attention, Cancelled: stopped. The details explain why.
messages.help.howitworks.when_something_fails.deb: DebridPulse sorts failures by how far they reach, and only does what each one allows:
messages.help.howitworks.when_something_fails.tem: A temporary problem (a timeout, a busy server, a rate limit) is retried automatically. A download uses Download Error Retries and Retry Delay; a service that fails to resolve a download into something it can fetch, Network Sources included, uses Resolution Failure Retries and Retry Delay (minutes) under Settings → Downloads → Download Behavior & Limits → Advanced Settings. The wait grows with each attempt, up to about five minutes unless the server asks for longer.

A temporary problem (a timeout, a busy server, a rate limit) is retried automatically, a set number of times: a download after an error, and a service that fails to resolve a download into something it can fetch, Network Sources included. The wait grows with each attempt, up to about five minutes unless the server asks for longer.
messages.help.howitworks.when_something_fails.pro: A problem with one service (for example, its retries are used up, or it refuses this download) makes DebridPulse try the next service that can handle the download, if there is one. A service that only failed temporarily may be tried again later, but it does not replace a service that is working.
A problem with the download itself (the file no longer exists, the source is invalid) stops it, because no other service can fix that.
messages.help.howitworks.when_something_fails.oth: Other sources for a file found by DebridPulse are used only when it can confirm they hold the same file, for example the same size and matching content or checksum. It never assumes two files match because of their names or positions. Alternatives you list yourself on one Quick Add line are tried in order, each as a separate attempt.
messages.help.howitworks.when_something_fails.sta: Stalled downloads: a download that makes no progress for the Stalled Download Timeout is stopped and retried, and a service that makes no progress preparing a download for that long counts as a failure of that service.
messages.help.howitworks.when_something_fails.swi: Switching to another source or service does not always keep the progress already made. Whether a partly finished file can be continued depends on the engine and the source, so a switch may start that file again.
messages.help.howitworks.switching_service_source: A download stays the same download when its service or its source changes. The service is who obtains the files (for example a debrid service or plain HTTPS); the source is where they come from (for example a particular file-hoster link). DebridPulse can know several sources that it has confirmed hold the same file, and these are two separate choices. Both controls appear only where you are allowed to change the download.

Choosing a service: on a row in Download Activity or Downloads, click the service name to open the Provider picker, or Provider for this transfer when the download has several links (in the download's details, each file's service name opens the picker for that file's link). The picker lists the services that claim at least one of the download's sources, not only the link in use, with each one's state (for example Current, Ready, Preparing…, Waiting for selection, Retrying… or Unavailable, with the reason); for a download of several links it says how many of its links each service can take. Switch is enabled only where that service can be chosen now. For several links the choice is best effort: each link switches on its own, and links a service cannot take stay where they are.

What a service switch does: if the chosen service can take the link in use, the download moves to it straight away and that file's download restarts there (Waiting for provider shows while the service gets it ready). If the service can reach a file only through another source DebridPulse has confirmed holds the same file, the file keeps downloading where it is and Preparing … appears beside the service name until that copy is ready; it then moves over once. If that service cannot provide it, the file simply stays where it is.

Choosing a source: the network button with a number opens the source chooser. For one file it lists that file's sources (N sources available for this file); for several files it lists Common sources and switches the remaining files. Choose Switch to this source; the one in use is marked ACTIVE, and a source that cannot be chosen now says Not currently switchable.

The service shown is the one committed. A switch that has not taken effect is shown beside it, never as it: Switching to … while your request is being made, Preparing … while a service prepares its copy.

Not every choice is accepted. Just before switching, DebridPulse checks again. If a link changed or was busy in the meantime, or a service cannot take it, that link is not switched and a message says so (for example No link was switched to …, with the reason). Nothing else changes, and you can try again once the list has refreshed. A refused switch, or a service that later fails, does not fail the download: the usual retries and fallbacks described above continue.

Why the choices change: a source that fails for good, a service that is switched off, unavailable, out of quota or not included in your plan, or a download that has finished drops out of the lists or is shown as unavailable. Switching back and forth does not by itself remove a choice.

Progress: when choosing a source would throw away progress already made, DebridPulse asks Discard downloaded progress? first. A service switch that would throw away progress is refused instead, with the reason would discard downloaded data; switch its source to confirm.

While a download is paused: choosing another source for a file that had already started downloading is accepted and saved, but nothing starts. The service and source shown stay the current ones, and beside the service name a message names where the file will go, for example Switch to Real-Debrid (rapidgator.net) on resume. Choosing again replaces it; choosing the source already in use removes it. After you resume it reads Switching to … until the switch has taken effect, then disappears. If the paused files of a download would go to different places, or the destination is not known, no destination is shown. A file that never started has nothing to hand over, so its new source simply applies when it starts. Choosing a service while paused works as described above, except that the download stays paused: a service that can take the link in use takes over at once (the badge shows it), and one that must first prepare a copy shows Preparing … and takes over only after you resume. These messages appear on the Download Activity and Downloads rows; both kinds can appear at once.
messages.help.howitworks.backup_torrents.each_deb: Each debrid service has a Prepare Backup Torrents switch. It is on by default for AllDebrid, Debrid-Link, Premiumize and Real-Debrid, and off by default for TorBox, whose torrent limits are tighter. While it is on, that service also adds torrents another service is delivering, so it is ready to take over if needed, and when you switch a download to another service, the torrent it already started is kept as a backup instead of being removed. This uses that account's torrent slots and limits; a new download that needs a slot takes it back first. Turn it off to keep that service's slots for its own downloads: its backups are then removed. A choice you already saved is kept.
messages.help.howitworks.backup_torrents.debrid_s: A debrid service can also add torrents another service is delivering, so it is ready to take over if needed, and when a download switches to another service, the torrent it already started can be kept as a backup instead of being removed. This is each service's Prepare Backup Torrents setting: on by default for AllDebrid, Debrid-Link, Premiumize and Real-Debrid, and off by default for TorBox, in that service's Additional Settings, part of the Advanced presentation. Backups use that account's torrent slots and limits; a new download that needs a slot takes it back first.

A debrid service can also add torrents another service is delivering, so it is ready to take over if needed, and when a download switches to another service, the torrent it already started can be kept as a backup instead of being removed. This is each service's Prepare Backup Torrents setting: on by default for AllDebrid, Debrid-Link, Premiumize and Real-Debrid, and off by default for TorBox. Backups use that account's torrent slots and limits; a new download that needs a slot takes it back first.
messages.help.howitworks.pause_resume_retry.pause: Pause holds one download; it does not occupy a download slot while paused. Resume lets it continue.
Pause All pauses every download and starts no new work, but still accepts new submissions. Resume All resumes everything.
messages.help.howitworks.pause_resume_retry.retry: Retry (or Reset) starts a failed download again from its original source, without re-adding it. On a finished or removed download it downloads the files again.
messages.help.howitworks.pause_resume_retry.recov: Recover All re-checks all tracked work with your services and engines and continues whatever can safely continue. It does not reset retry counts or override your settings.
messages.help.howitworks.pause_resume_retry.remov: Remove takes a download off the list. DebridPulse also cleans up the copy it created at the service and any unfinished partial files it was writing. Files that finished downloading stay in your folder.
messages.help.howitworks.pause_resume_retry.admin: An Admin can remove, cancel or switch the source of any download. A User can do so only when no other account still needs that download, including downloads merged into it; otherwise the User withdraws their own request in Requested By, and the download continues for the others.
messages.help.howitworks.adding_same_thing.if_add: If you add a magnet, {file_type}, NZB or Metalink file that DebridPulse is already working on (including one that failed and has not been removed), it shows Already in queue and keeps the existing download instead of starting a second one. Web links are always added as a new download. Once a download is finished, cancelled or removed, adding the same source again starts a new download. When two downloads turn out to fetch the same content, DebridPulse may merge them; the merged one shows Consolidated. When DebridPulse cannot prove that they match, the merged one shows Consolidated · Unverified instead. Merging does not change who asked for it: each account's request stays its own.
messages.help.howitworks.what_survives_restart.do: Downloads, their history, the queue order, Pause All and the speed cap are saved and survive a restart; DebridPulse reconnects to its engines and continues. Browser sign-ins do not survive a restart, so you sign in again. Passwords typed into a prompt or written into a link are never saved and are forgotten on restart.
A username and password written into a link ({link}) are used for that download instead of asking, including for every file in a folder, and are removed from the link before it is saved. They are kept only in memory for that download, and are forgotten when it finishes, is cancelled or removed, after at most 24 hours, or when DebridPulse restarts.

For SFTP, SCP and SSH servers, DebridPulse confirms the server's identity before sending any password. A rejected password is never retried automatically; DebridPulse asks again. Media Downloads never uses passwords.
messages.help.services.title: Services and sources
messages.help.services.summary.admin: What each service in Settings → Services is for, what it needs, and what to expect from it.
messages.help.services.summary.member: What each service DebridPulse can use is for, and what to expect from it.
messages.help.services.lead.settings_services_has: Settings → Services has two groups. Premium Services need your own account with an outside service. Network Sources download directly from a server and need no account with anyone (although the server itself may ask for a password).
messages.help.services.who_sets_up.admin_connects: An Admin connects and configures services in Settings. The descriptions below explain what each one does and what to expect from it.
messages.help.services.how_service_card.enable: Enable switches the service on or off immediately.
messages.help.services.how_service_card.status_wo: The status word says whether it is Unconfigured (switched on but not connected), Unverified (connected, but the current settings have not passed a Test) or Verified.
messages.help.services.how_service_card.test: Test checks the saved connection. A passing Test means the account and settings worked at that moment; it does not guarantee that every link or plan feature will work later.
messages.help.services.how_service_card.additiona: Additional Settings holds optional tuning. The defaults suit most people. Each debrid service's Prepare Backup Torrents is explained under How It Works → Backup torrents.
messages.help.services.how_service_card.each_card: Each card's optional tuning (Additional Settings) keeps its saved values and is part of the Advanced presentation. The defaults suit most people.
messages.help.services.how_service_card.while_ser: While a service still has downloads in progress, DebridPulse will not let you change its account (or, for Usenet, its news servers); finish or remove those downloads first.
messages.help.services.how_service_card.help_butt: The Help button (?) on a card explains that card in Settings itself.
messages.help.services.alldebrid.for: For: magnets, {file_type} files and links to file hosters AllDebrid supports.
messages.help.services.alldebrid.need: You need: an AllDebrid account and its API key, from AllDebrid's API key page. Paste it into API Key; it is saved when you leave the field and then shows Key present. Remove API Key deletes it.
messages.help.services.alldebrid.what_happens: What happens: AllDebrid fetches the content on its own servers, then DebridPulse downloads the files from AllDebrid with aria2. Your computer never joins a torrent swarm. For a multi-file torrent you can choose files.
messages.help.services.alldebrid.good_know.provid: Good to know: off by default, like every premium service. With a free account, only hosts AllDebrid offers to free users can be used, and torrents are refused. Maximum Active Torrents left empty follows AllDebrid's own limit; per AllDebrid's documentation that is 30 active magnets.

Good to know: off by default, like every premium service. With a free account, only hosts AllDebrid offers to free users can be used, and torrents are refused. Per AllDebrid's documentation, an account can have up to 30 active magnets.
messages.help.services.alldebrid.if_fails: If it fails: a Test error usually means a wrong or revoked key. A torrent refused on a free account needs a premium account or another service.
messages.help.services.debrid_link.for: For: magnets, {file_type} files (through your Debrid-Link seedbox) and links to supported file hosters.
messages.help.services.debrid_link.need: You need: a Debrid-Link account and its API key, pasted into API Key.
messages.help.services.debrid_link.what_happens: What happens: Debrid-Link prepares the files; DebridPulse downloads them with aria2. A hoster link that contains several files offers file selection.
messages.help.services.debrid_link.good_know.prov: Good to know: off by default. The supported host list is refreshed every 24 hours by default (Supported Host Refresh Interval). What your account may use depends on your Debrid-Link plan: DebridPulse only uses torrents on an account it can confirm is premium, and on a free account only hosts Debrid-Link marks as free.

Good to know: off by default. The supported host list is refreshed every 24 hours by default. What your account may use depends on your Debrid-Link plan: DebridPulse only uses torrents on an account it can confirm is premium, and on a free account only hosts Debrid-Link marks as free.
messages.help.services.debrid_link.if_fails: If it fails: check the API key with Test, and the download's details for an account or quota message.
messages.help.services.premiumize.for: For: magnets, {file_type} files, NZBs and links to supported file hosters.
messages.help.services.premiumize.need: You need: a Premiumize premium account and its API key, pasted into API Key.
messages.help.services.premiumize.what_happens: What happens: DebridPulse first asks Premiumize for immediate download links. If that is not possible, it adds the item to your Premiumize cloud storage and downloads it from there once ready. Files are downloaded with aria2.
messages.help.services.premiumize.good_know.provi: Good to know: off by default. A free or expired Premiumize account stays connected but cannot start anything. For NZBs, Premiumize is normally tried after your own Usenet servers; switch on Use Premiumize Before Usenet to try it first. Either way both stay in the running: if the first cannot take the NZB, the other is tried.

Good to know: off by default. A free or expired Premiumize account stays connected but cannot start anything. For NZBs, Premiumize is normally tried after your own Usenet servers, unless it is set to go first. Either way both stay in the running: if the first cannot take the NZB, the other is tried.
messages.help.services.premiumize.premiumize_news: Premiumize as a news server: per Premiumize's documentation, a Premiumize account also includes Usenet access that you can add as an ordinary news server under Usenet with Add Server. Take the server details from Premiumize's own instructions. That server is separate from this card.
messages.help.services.premiumize.if_fails: If it fails: an account limit or fair-use message is treated as temporary and DebridPulse may try another service.
messages.help.services.real_debrid.for: For: magnets, {file_type} files and links to supported file hosters.
messages.help.services.real_debrid.need: You need: a Real-Debrid account. There is no key to paste. Press Connect Real-Debrid; DebridPulse shows a code. Press Open Real-Debrid, sign in on Real-Debrid's site and enter the code (Copy copies it). The card then shows Connected as your account name. Connecting is your choice to use the account, so Real-Debrid is switched on as soon as the new connection is proven to work; a later Test never switches it on.
messages.help.services.real_debrid.what_happens: What happens: Real-Debrid fetches the content; DebridPulse downloads the files with aria2.
messages.help.services.real_debrid.good_know.prov: Good to know: the code expires after a while; press Connect again for a new one. Disconnect makes DebridPulse forget the authorization and also asks Real-Debrid to cancel it. With a free account, torrents are refused and only free hosts work. Per Real-Debrid's documentation it allows at most 250 requests a minute; API Calls per Minute defaults to 240.

Good to know: the code expires after a while; press Connect again for a new one. Disconnect makes DebridPulse forget the authorization and also asks Real-Debrid to cancel it. With a free account, torrents are refused and only free hosts work. Per Real-Debrid's documentation it allows at most 250 requests a minute.
messages.help.services.real_debrid.if_fails: If it fails: if the card says it is not connected, connect again.
messages.help.services.torbox.for: For: magnets, {file_type} files, links to supported file hosters and, depending on your plan, NZBs.
messages.help.services.torbox.need: You need: a TorBox account. Like Real-Debrid, it uses a code instead of a key: press Connect TorBox, then Open TorBox and approve the code there. TorBox is switched on as soon as the new connection is proven to work; a later Test never switches it on.
messages.help.services.torbox.what_happens: What happens: TorBox fetches the content; DebridPulse downloads the files with aria2. TorBox can report whether something is already available on its side, which lets it be tried first.
messages.help.services.torbox.plan_matters.provid: Your plan matters: a free TorBox plan stays connected, but TorBox refuses the downloads DebridPulse asks for on it, so DebridPulse starts nothing there; per TorBox's documentation, the paid plans include torrents and web downloads, and only the Pro plan includes NZB downloads. DebridPulse follows what TorBox reports for your account: if it is known not to include Usenet, switching on Use TorBox Before Usenet is refused with Requires TorBox Pro. That switch only changes the order for NZBs; TorBox still handles NZBs as a fallback when your plan allows it. Maximum Active Torrents left empty follows your plan's limit.

Your plan matters: a free TorBox plan stays connected, but TorBox refuses the downloads DebridPulse asks for on it, so DebridPulse starts nothing there; per TorBox's documentation, the paid plans include torrents and web downloads, and only the Pro plan includes NZB downloads. DebridPulse follows what TorBox reports for your account; NZBs go to TorBox only when your plan allows it.
messages.help.services.torbox.good_know: Good to know: Disconnect only makes DebridPulse forget the token. TorBox offers no way to cancel it remotely, so reset your token on TorBox's website if you want it revoked there.
messages.help.services.usenet.for: For: NZB files. An NZB is a small file that lists the parts of a Usenet posting; Usenet is a network of news servers, usually reached through a paid news server subscription.
messages.help.services.usenet.need: You need: at least one news server account. Press Add Server and fill in Host, Port (563 by default), SSL (on by default), Username and Password. Under Advanced you can set Connections, Priority (lower values have priority; 0 is the highest), Articles per Request and Server Timeout. Press the server's own Test to check it, and the pencil to give it a display name.
messages.help.services.usenet.what_happens: What happens: DebridPulse runs its own private SABnzbd download engine for Usenet; there is nothing to install or sign in to. It downloads the posting, checks it and repairs it with the posting's repair files when needed. Extraction is done afterwards by DebridPulse's own Automatic Extraction, using your Archive Passwords.
messages.help.services.usenet.good_know.transfer_: Good to know: Usenet is off by default and counts as set up only when at least one enabled server has a host and at least one connection. It shows Verified only when every such server has passed a Test with its current settings. NZB files are added through Quick Add; there is no file selection. Global Usenet settings are under Settings → Downloads → Transfer Method Settings → Usenet, and the Usenet card's own Help button explains its settings.
messages.help.services.usenet.good_know.admin: Good to know: Usenet is off by default and counts as set up only when at least one enabled server has a host and at least one connection. It shows Verified only when every such server has passed a Test with its current settings. NZB files are added through Quick Add; there is no file selection. The Usenet card's own Help button explains its settings.
messages.help.services.usenet.good_know.member: Good to know: Usenet is off by default and counts as set up only when at least one enabled server has a host and at least one connection. It shows Verified only when every such server has passed a Test with its current settings. NZB files are added through Quick Add; there is no file selection.
messages.help.services.usenet.if_fails: If it fails: the header Test reports how many servers passed. If a posting is incomplete on your servers, a server with longer retention or different coverage may have the missing parts.
messages.help.services.network_sources.all_networ: All network sources are switched on in a new installation. The group's Enable turns the whole group off or back on; each box also has its own, and a source works only while both are on. Turning the group back on restores each box as it was. They have no Test button: whether a link works depends on that server. Their tuning is under Settings → Downloads → Transfer Method Settings.

All network sources are switched on in a new installation. The group's Enable turns the whole group off or back on; each box also has its own, and a source works only while both are on. Turning the group back on restores each box as it was. They have no Test button: whether a link works depends on that server.
All network sources are switched on in a new installation, and need no account with anyone. Whether a link works depends on that server.
messages.help.services.https.ordinary_web_links.t: Ordinary web links ({link_1} and {link_2}) that no specialist service claims. Each link is one file, downloaded with aria2. A server that needs a password asks for one, or you can write it into the link. Tuning: Transfer Method Settings → Network Sources.

Ordinary web links ({link_1} and {link_2}) that no specialist service claims. Each link is one file, downloaded with aria2. A server that needs a password asks for one, or you can write it into the link.
messages.help.services.sftp.ftp_sftp_links: {link_1} and {link_2} links to a file or a folder. A folder means the files directly inside it (no subfolders), offered in file selection. Sign-in is by username and password; SFTP asks you to confirm the server's identity first. Downloaded with aria2.
messages.help.services.scp.scp_ssh_links: {link_1} and {link_2} links to one file ({link_3}), the files directly inside a folder ({link_4}), or the files in one folder matching a pattern in the last part of the path ({link_5}; only {literal_1} and {literal_2}). Subfolders are never entered. A path starting {path_1} starts in your login folder; another user's {path_2} and patterns in folder names are not accepted.
messages.help.services.scp.files_downloaded_over: Files are downloaded over SFTP with aria2, so the server must offer SFTP. Sign-in is by username and password, after confirming the server's identity.
messages.help.services.rsync.rsync_host_path: {link_1} names a file or folder on an rsync server; {link_2} lists the server's shared areas. DebridPulse asks the rsync service first. If it does not share that path, or does not answer within Connection Timeout, the same path is read over SSH instead. A link with its own port always means that rsync service, and {link_3} always means SSH.
messages.help.services.rsync.folder_includes_subf: A folder includes its subfolders, down to the Directory Depth you choose (all levels by default), and opens file selection. Links on the server are never followed and names are taken literally (no wildcards). rsync only reads from the server; it never changes, deletes or uploads anything there.
messages.help.services.rsync.over_ssh_server.tran: Over SSH, the server's identity is confirmed first and you sign in with a password or a key file (and its passphrase). An rsync service's shared areas may ask for their own password. Downloaded by DebridPulse's rsync engine. Tuning: Transfer Method Settings → rsync.

Over SSH, the server's identity is confirmed first and you sign in with a password or a key file (and its passphrase). An rsync service's shared areas may ask for their own password. Downloaded by DebridPulse's rsync engine.
messages.help.services.webdav.webdavs_davs_links: {link_1} or {link_2} links (or {link_3} and {link_4} for a server without HTTPS) to a file or folder on a WebDAV server, a common way to share files from cloud storage and NAS devices. A plain {link_5} or {link_6} link ending in {path} (with no {literal} query) is tried as WebDAV first and becomes an ordinary download if the server does not offer WebDAV there.
messages.help.services.webdav.folder_opens_file.t: A folder opens file selection with the files directly inside it; Directory Depth adds subfolder levels. A folder with more files than Maximum Files, or whose files cannot all be found within Collection Scan Timeout (no limit by default), is not added at all rather than added in part. A protected server asks for its password once per server for that download, not once for every file. Files are downloaded with aria2. Tuning: Transfer Method Settings → WebDAV.

A folder opens file selection with the files directly inside it; Directory Depth adds subfolder levels. A folder with more files than Maximum Files, or whose files cannot all be found within Collection Scan Timeout (no limit by default), is not added at all rather than added in part. A protected server asks for its password once per server for that download, not once for every file. Files are downloaded with aria2.
messages.help.services.metalink_multimeta.reads_m: Reads Metalink files: an uploaded {file_type_1} file, or a web link ending in {file_type_2}. A Metalink file lists one or more files with several download addresses for each. Each address is downloaded through whichever service handles it, in the order the publisher prefers; if one fails, the next listed address is used. A declared size or checksum is checked when the file completes. A Metalink file describing several files opens file selection. Older Metalink 3 files are not supported, and links to other metadata (such as torrents) inside a Metalink file are not followed.
messages.help.services.media_downloads.downloads_: Downloads video and audio from web pages on sites the bundled yt-dlp media downloader recognises, for example many popular video sites. A link to a page yt-dlp does not specifically recognise stays an ordinary HTTP(S) download.
messages.help.services.media_downloads.what_get: What you get: one file per item, named {literal}, in the site's own format when possible and otherwise MKV. Video and audio are combined without re-encoding, so quality is not reduced. Title, description and date are written into the file, and one subtitle in your Preferred Subtitle Language is embedded when the site offers it.
messages.help.services.media_downloads.choices.tr: Choices: Target Resolution, Video Quality and Preferred Video Codec choose among the versions the site offers; DebridPulse never converts media. Settings are under Transfer Method Settings → Media Downloads.
Choices: the saved resolution, quality and codec preferences choose among the versions the site offers; DebridPulse never converts media.
messages.help.services.media_downloads.playlists: Playlists: up to the first 100 entries. A video link that is also part of a playlist asks whether you want the Current Video or the Playlist.
messages.help.services.media_downloads.not_suppor: Not supported: media that needs a sign-in, cookies or a subscription; live or upcoming streams; DRM-protected media; and media on your local network.
messages.help.services.media_downloads.good_know: Good to know: an interrupted media download starts that item again from the beginning.
messages.help.engines.title: Download engines
messages.help.engines.summary: The programs that write files to your storage. DebridPulse includes and runs all of them; there is nothing to install or connect.
messages.help.engines.lead.service_decides_where: A service decides where files come from; an engine does the downloading. DebridPulse picks the engine that fits each file, so one download can use different engines over its life, for example after switching to another service.
messages.help.engines.aria2.downloads_web_http: Downloads web (HTTP and HTTPS), FTP and SFTP files. It handles files from debrid services, HTTP(S), (S)FTP, SCP, WebDAV and most Metalink addresses. aria2 in DebridPulse cannot share torrents, so it never uploads to anyone.
messages.help.engines.aria2.admin_sidebar_shows: For an Admin, the sidebar shows aria2: offline when it is not responding.
messages.help.engines.rsync.downloads_rsync_links: Downloads rsync links, both from rsync services and over SSH. With Partial Transfers on (the default) it can continue a partly downloaded file, and it only ever reads from the server.
messages.help.engines.usenet_sabnzbd.private_copy: A private copy of SABnzbd that DebridPulse runs for NZB downloads from your news servers. It downloads and repairs postings but does not unpack them; Automatic Extraction does that.
messages.help.engines.media_downloads_yt.download: Downloads media from supported sites in an isolated process and combines video, audio and subtitles without re-encoding. It cannot continue an interrupted item; that item starts again.
messages.help.engines.limits_apply_every.maximum_: Maximum Concurrent Downloads (Settings → Downloads → Download Behavior & Limits, 3 by default) is one limit for all engines together.
messages.help.engines.limits_apply_every.speed_ca: The speed cap in the header is shared between the engines that are downloading at that moment, and together they never exceed it. An engine that needs less keeps what it uses and the rest goes to the engines that can use it; engines that all want more share it equally. An engine with work waiting keeps a small part, so it can never start above the cap.
messages.help.engines.limits_apply_every.disk_spa: Disk Space & Recovery settings (free space, retries, stalled downloads) apply to every engine.
messages.help.engines.limits_apply_every.free_spa: The free-space guard, retries and stalled-download recovery apply to every engine.
messages.help.engines.tuning_aria2_transfer.conne: Connections per Server and Segments per File: how many connections and pieces one file may use at once.
messages.help.engines.tuning_aria2_transfer.minim: Minimum Split Size: the smallest piece a file is split into; larger values mean fewer, bigger pieces.
messages.help.engines.tuning_aria2_transfer.conti: Continue Partial Downloads: continue a partly downloaded file instead of starting again, when the server allows it.
messages.help.engines.tuning_aria2_transfer.lowes: Lowest Speed Limit: drops a connection that stays slower than this; {literal} turns it off.
messages.help.engines.tuning_aria2_transfer.disk_: Disk Cache: memory used to reduce disk writes.
messages.help.engines.tuning_aria2_transfer.file_: File Allocation: how disk space is reserved for a new file.
messages.help.engines.tuning_aria2_transfer.more_: More connections do not guarantee more speed: the server, the service, your network or your disk can each be the limit. Change one setting at a time.
messages.help.engines.tuning_rsync_usenet.rsync: rsync: Partial Transfers, Compression, Preserve Modification Time, Connection Timeout, Transfer Timeout and Directory Depth.
messages.help.engines.tuning_rsync_usenet.usenet: Usenet: Article Cache Limit, Maximum Retries (for each part of a posting, separate from DebridPulse's own download retries), Request Timeout and Direct Write. Settings for each news server are on its card under Services.
messages.help.engines.tuning_rsync_usenet.media_d: Media Downloads: Target Resolution, Video Quality, Preferred Video Codec, Preferred Subtitle Language, Concurrent Fragment Downloads (pieces of one streamed video fetched at once) and YouTube Player Clients (empty is Automatic, yt-dlp's own choice; a different choice can change the formats offered and does not guarantee passing a YouTube sign-in check).
messages.help.engines.download_engine_activity.se: Settings → Downloads → Download Engine Activity lists the engines' jobs (filter by Active, Waiting, Paused or Stopped), with Pause, Resume or Terminate where that engine supports it. Terminate asks first. It is a recovery tool for a job that is truly stuck. For normal work, use the Downloads page, which keeps DebridPulse's own records in step.
messages.help.settings.title: Settings reference
messages.help.settings.summary.server_advanced: The seven Settings tabs, their cards, and the options most people need. Settings is available to Admins.
messages.help.settings.how_saving_works.there_no_: There is no Save button. Every setting is saved on its own: a typed value is saved when you leave the field, and a switch or list choice is saved the moment you change it. If a value cannot be saved, a message explains why and the field returns to its saved value.
messages.help.settings.how_saving_works.stored_se: Stored secrets such as API keys and passwords are never shown again. When one is stored, the field shows that it is set, and leaving it blank keeps the stored value. To delete a secret, use its Remove or Clear button and confirm.
messages.help.settings.how_saving_works.test: Test buttons save any field you are still editing, then check the saved settings.
messages.help.settings.how_saving_works.every_car: Every card has a Help button (?) in its header that explains that card in more detail. This manual is the complete reference; the card help is a summary where you need it.
Premium Services: one card each for Usenet, AllDebrid, Debrid-Link, Premiumize, Real-Debrid and TorBox, with Enable, Test, the account connection and Additional Settings.

Premium Services: one card each for Usenet, AllDebrid, Debrid-Link, Premiumize, Real-Debrid and TorBox, with Enable, Test and the account connection. Each service's Additional Settings keep their saved values and are part of the Advanced presentation.
messages.help.settings.services.network_sources: Network Sources: one Enable for the group and one for each of HTTP(S), (S)FTP, SCP, rsync, WebDAV, Metalink (Multimeta) and Media Downloads.
messages.help.settings.services.services_tab_manu: The Services tab of this manual explains each one.
messages.help.settings.downloads.download_behavio: Download Behavior & Limits: Download Folder (with Browse) and Maximum Concurrent Downloads. Under Advanced Settings: Material Checkpoint Interval and Graceful Stop Timeout (best left alone), Local Network Connections (off by default) to allow downloads from devices on your private network, and Skip Local Connection Confirmation to stop asking each time. Even when allowed, DebridPulse never connects to the computer it runs on or other non-private local addresses. Also there: Provider Poll Interval (how often a service is checked for progress on work it is preparing), Full Sync Interval (how often downloads are reconciled with every enabled premium account that lists its transfers; 0 turns it off), and Resolution Failure Retries with Retry Delay (minutes) (how often and how soon a failed resolution is tried again, for any service including Network Sources).
messages.help.settings.downloads.transfer_method_: Transfer Method Settings: tuning for Network Sources (aria2), rsync, WebDAV, Usenet and Media Downloads. See the Engines and Services tabs of this manual.
messages.help.settings.downloads.disk_space_recov: Disk Space & Recovery: Minimum Free Disk Space (0 turns the guard off) holds new downloads when free space falls below it; Resume Free Space Buffer is how much extra must be free before they continue, so downloads do not stop and start repeatedly. Download Error Retries, Retry Delay and Stalled Download Timeout (0 turns it off) control automatic recovery.
messages.help.settings.downloads.download_engine_: Download Engine Activity: the engines' current jobs, for troubleshooting only.
messages.help.settings.downloads.download_behavio: Download Behavior & Limits: Download Folder (with Browse) and Maximum Concurrent Downloads.
messages.help.settings.downloads.rest_tab_advance: The rest of this tab -- the Advanced Settings of Download Behavior & Limits, Transfer Method Settings, Disk Space & Recovery and Download Engine Activity -- is part of the Advanced presentation. Those settings keep working with their saved values: retries, the free-space guard and each transfer method's tuning are not reset or turned off.
messages.help.settings.extraction.automatic_extra: The Automatic Extraction card unpacks archives after a download finishes. It is off by default.
messages.help.settings.extraction.concurrent_extr: Concurrent Extractions: how many archives are unpacked at once.
messages.help.settings.extraction.delete_archives: Delete Archives After Extraction (on by default): removes the archive only after it was unpacked successfully.
messages.help.settings.extraction.archive_passwor: Archive Passwords: for a 7z or RAR archive, DebridPulse tries no password first, then each stored password in order. A ZIP archive is extracted without a password only; these passwords are not tried for ZIP. Each row holds one password; it is saved when you leave the row. Show all reveals them; Clear Passwords erases the whole list.
messages.help.settings.extraction.supported_forma: Supported formats include ZIP, 7z, RAR (including multi-part RAR), TAR with gzip, bzip2, xz, zstd or lzma compression, and single gzip, bzip2 or xz files. Archives that would write outside the download folder, contain links, or would be unreasonably large when unpacked are refused for your safety.
messages.help.settings.signing.standalone_install: A Standalone installation has no Authentication tab. Its built-in Administrator, the only person who can sign in, signs in with a password alone, set, changed or cleared in My Account: with a password, the sign-in page asks for it, with no username; without one, no sign-in is required and anyone who can reach DebridPulse uses it as the Administrator. OpenID Connect is not available.
messages.help.settings.signing.when_sign_promethe: When sign-in is on, the Prometheus metrics address {path} also needs a credential; give your monitoring tool an Integration token from Access & Integrations.
messages.help.settings.authentication.authenticat: Authentication Status: the current mode, the state of each sign-in method, Active Browser Sessions with Log Out Current Session, and Browser Session Lifetime (12 hours by default).
messages.help.settings.authentication.turning_use: Turning Username & Password or OpenID Connect on or off, and changing their settings, are done in their own cards, which are part of the Advanced presentation: choose Advanced in My Account to show them. Sign-in keeps working exactly as configured.
messages.help.settings.authentication.when_sign_p: When sign-in is on, the Prometheus metrics address {path} also needs a credential; give your monitoring tool an Integration token from Users & Access.
messages.help.settings.authentication.username_pa: Username & Password: Enable turns password sign-in on for everyone, and needs an active Admin with a password. The Username and Password fields are your own account's; other people's are managed in Users & Access. The same username and password also work for scripts that use HTTP Basic sign-in.
messages.help.settings.authentication.openid_conn: OpenID Connect (OIDC): sign in through an identity service you already run, such as Authentik or Keycloak. Set Public DebridPulse Base URL to the HTTPS address people use to reach DebridPulse; DebridPulse then shows the exact OIDC Callback URL to register with your identity service. Fill in Issuer URL, Client ID and, if needed, Client Secret, then press Test, which runs a real sign-in in a pop-up window. Access Control decides who may sign in: with Allow Any Authenticated OIDC Identity on, anyone your identity service signs in is admitted; with it off, a person must match every list that is filled in: Allowed Subjects (written {literal_1}), Allowed Emails (the email must be verified, {literal_2}) and Allowed Groups (read from the Group Claim). If every list is empty, no one can sign in through OIDC. Default Role for New OIDC Users (User or ReadOnly User) is the role an identity receives the first time it signs in; OIDC never creates an Admin. A new OIDC identity always gets its own account; it is never joined to an existing account just because the email matches. If the base URL is set by the {literal_3} environment variable, the field is read-only here; change it in your installation instead.
messages.help.settings.authentication.turning_off: Turning off the last sign-in method asks for confirmation, because it leaves DebridPulse open to anyone who can reach it. Failed sign-ins are slowed down rather than locked out.
messages.help.settings.authentication.when_sign_p: When sign-in is on, the Prometheus metrics address {path} also needs a credential; give your monitoring tool an Integration token from Users & Access (an Admin's HTTP Basic credentials also work).
messages.help.settings.access_integrations.deploy: Deployment Type, first on this tab, shows that this installation is Standalone and switches it to Server after a confirmation; its Help button says what each type keeps and changes.
messages.help.settings.access_integrations.only_b: Only the built-in Administrator can sign in to a Standalone installation. Other people's accounts, kept from a time this installation was a Server, are not deleted or converted: they keep their data but cannot sign in while it is Standalone. Standalone has no User Accounts card; they are managed again once the installation is a Server.
messages.help.settings.access_integrations.integr: Integration accounts keep working as before: an external application, not a person, that cannot sign in to these pages; with its API tokens it can add downloads through the API, submit and follow its own jobs through the external-client and download-client interfaces, and read metrics.

Integration Accounts are for automation and cannot sign in to these pages. Issue Token shows a new token once, so copy it then; tools send it as {literal}. Each token sees only the jobs submitted with it. Revoke stops a token at once without touching anything it already submitted.

Integration Delivery Profiles tell an external application, such as Sonarr or Radarr, which categories it may submit to, which kinds of source it may send (Source Types), which of its tokens may use the profile (Authorized API Tokens), and where it will find the finished files (DP Download Path in DebridPulse's download folder, and External Import Path as the application sees that folder). Files are shared in place: nothing is copied, moved or deleted for the application. The download-client interfaces stay unavailable until a profile has a category, a Source Type and an authorized API token that is active.
messages.help.settings.access_integrations.admini: The Administrator changes its display name, actual name and email, sets, changes or clears its password, and chooses Easy or Advanced in My Account.
messages.help.settings.users_access.every_account: Every account has one of four fixed roles:
messages.help.settings.users_access.admin: Admin: everything, including Settings, the Activity Log and every transfer.
messages.help.settings.users_access.user: User: adds downloads and pauses, resumes, retries and reorders them; sees every transfer; can remove, cancel or switch a download only when no other account still needs it, and otherwise withdraws their own request. Has their own Notifications page; Settings are not available.
messages.help.settings.users_access.readonly_user: ReadOnly User: sees the Dashboard, Downloads, Details and Statistics, and changes nothing in downloads or settings; its own profile and presentation in My Account remain its own to change.
messages.help.settings.users_access.integration: Integration: an external application, not a person. It cannot sign in to these pages; with its API tokens it can add downloads through the API, submit and follow its own jobs through the external-client and download-client interfaces, and read metrics.
